content.user_title: Analyze Molecules with Datamol and RDKit
content.value_statement: Cheminformatics workflows can be slow to assemble with raw RDKit APIs. This skill guides Datamol tasks for parsing, descriptors, fingerprints, visualization, conformers, and reactions.
actual_capabilities: Guides conversion among SMILES, InChI, SELFIES, SMARTS, and RDKit Mol objects.
Explains sanitization, standardization, metal disconnection, normalization, and hydrogen handling with Datamol.
Supports descriptor, fingerprint, similarity, clustering, and diversity selection workflows.
Covers SDF, SMILES, CSV, Excel, Parquet, JSON, and remote path I/O through Datamol.
Helps plan 3D conformer generation, RMSD clustering, SASA calculation, and conformer visualization.
Provides reaction, scaffold, fragmentation, visualization, and machine learning feature guidance.
limitations: It does not replace RDKit when advanced parameter control is required.
It depends on Datamol, RDKit, and optional storage libraries being installed in the user environment.
Very large clustering jobs can exceed memory because full distance matrices may be built.
Remote I/O examples require user-approved paths and appropriate cloud credentials.

use_cases.title: Clean Compound Libraries
use_cases.description: Standardize SMILES, remove invalid molecules, and prepare clean tables for downstream descriptor and fingerprint analysis.

use_cases.title: Compare Structure Series
use_cases.description: Group molecules by scaffold, visualize aligned analogs, and review descriptor trends for a structure activity series.

use_cases.title: Prepare ML Features
use_cases.description: Create molecular fingerprints or descriptor matrices, plan scaffold splits, and reduce leakage in predictive modeling workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Parse and Clean Molecules
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a small molecule list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Datamol to parse these SMILES, standardize valid molecules, and explain which entries fail: <SMILES list>.

prompt_templates.title: Compute Drug-Like Descriptors
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Datamol workflow for descriptor calculation, Lipinski filtering, and a clear table of failed criteria for <compound dataset>.

prompt_templates.title: Rank a Screening Library
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Datamol screening plan using fingerprints, similarity ranking, clustering, and visualization for <query compounds> against <library>.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare ML-Ready Features
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Datamol pipeline that standardizes structures, creates fingerprints, splits by scaffold, and reports leakage risks for <dataset>.

output_examples.input: A scientist asks for a drug-likeness review of a SMILES list.
output: The response recommends standardizing molecules before scoring.
It lists descriptors such as molecular weight, logP, hydrogen bond counts, TPSA, and aromatic atom counts.
It identifies likely filter failures and suggests reviewing salts, metals, and invalid SMILES.

output_examples.input: A chemist asks how to visualize an analog series.
output: The response recommends scaffold grouping and aligned molecule grids.
It suggests legends that include activity values or compound identifiers.
It notes that large grids should be saved to files instead of displayed in memory.

output_examples.input: An ML engineer asks for a training feature plan.
output: The response outlines structure standardization, fingerprint generation, and descriptor matrix creation.
It recommends scaffold-aware splitting to reduce structural leakage.
It flags memory limits for full pairwise distance matrices on large datasets.

best_practices: Standardize and sanitize external molecules before descriptors, fingerprints, clustering, or visualization.
Use parallel processing carefully, and set explicit worker counts for shared machines.
Use scaffold splits when building molecular machine learning benchmarks.
anti_patterns: Do not use full distance matrix clustering for very large compound libraries.
Do not trust invalid or unstandardized SMILES when comparing descriptors.
Do not use remote paths without confirming the data source and credentials.

faq.question: What is Datamol used for?
faq.answer: Datamol simplifies common RDKit workflows for molecular parsing, descriptors, fingerprints, visualization, conformers, and data I/O.

faq.question: Does this skill replace RDKit?
faq.answer: No. It helps with Datamol defaults, while advanced RDKit control may still require direct RDKit usage.

faq.question: Can it work with SMILES files and SDF files?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill covers Datamol readers and writers for SMILES, SDF, CSV, Excel, Parquet, JSON, and related formats.

faq.question: Can it help with 3D conformers?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers conformer generation, RMSD clustering, solvent accessible surface area, and conformer visualization.

faq.question: Is it suitable for large compound libraries?
faq.answer: It can help plan batch workflows, but some clustering and distance methods may exceed memory on large libraries.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
